title: How AI Got Here, episode 1: a bronze giant and a box of gears
summary: Before computers, people imagined thinking machines and built mechanical ones: the myth of Talos, the Antikythera mechanism and Hero of Alexandria's rope-programmed cart.
label: ANIMATED DOCUMENTARY · ILLUSTRATION
artCredit: Illustrations drawn in code by AI Broadsheet
ticker: HOW AI GOT HERE · EPISODE 1 OF 12 · FROM MYTH TO MACHINE

say: Long before computers, people dreamed of machines that could act on their own.
This is how AI got here.
In Greek myth, a bronze giant named Talos guarded the island of Crete.
He circled its shores three times a day, throwing rocks at approaching ships.
A single vein ran from his neck to his ankle, sealed by a bronze nail.
Pull the nail, and the machine stopped.
In 1901, divers raised lumps of corroded bronze from an ancient shipwreck off the Greek island of Antikythera.
Inside were at least 30 hand-cut bronze gears.
Turn its handle, and it tracked the sun and the moon, and predicted eclipses.
In the first century, Hero of Alexandria described a cart that moved on its own.
A falling weight pulled a rope wound around its axles, and pegs set where it turned.
Some computer scientists call it an early program.
Myth gave us the dream. Gears gave us the method.
